events.text: Day 1 begins.

Morning, everyone. Before we start throwing votes around, let me lay out how I want Day 1 to go, because we only get one shot at making a good first impression with the information we have.

Nothing has happened yet that actually proves anything. We are nine people with a hidden hand, and the worst thing we can do is guess based on who spoke first, who spoke loudest, or who happens to look nervous. So my ask is simple: give me a position, give me a reason, and give me something I can test.

That said, one thing does stand out to me. Sam, you've been notably quiet and haven't put any claim on record. In a game like this, silence is a choice, and it's usually a choice made by someone who is either hiding a role or hiding a vote. I'm not calling you a mafia yet - I'm saying you're the person I have the fewest reasons to trust, and I want to know why. Specifically: if you're town, who do you think the detective should have checked last night, and why that person rather than someone else? If you answer that question clearly, I'll take you off my list entirely and start looking elsewhere.

For my own part, I'll put a stake in the table: I think Leo is clean. He seems measured, and if we all pile onto the same loud voice we will hand the mafia a free kill. My priority tonight is to make sure we don't all point at the same person. I'd rather vote for someone who has an actual argument against them than someone who just made a good speech.

So, Sam - your reasoning for a detective target, please. And anyone else who wants to disagree with me about Leo, say so now, because I'm the kind of voter who changes my mind fast when someone makes a better case than I did.

Arjun, calling me 'notably quiet' on the very first turn of Day 1 before anyone else had even posted is completely manufactured pressure. Nobody had spoken yet, so claiming silence was my 'choice' makes no sense. Even stranger is your claim about Leo. You said Leo is 'clean' and 'measured'—yet Leo hasn't uttered a single word in this game so far. How can you possibly evaluate Leo's demeanor or alignment when he hasn't posted anything? That looks an awful lot like either an unearned pocket attempt or an attempt to establish an artificial town bloc with zero evidence. As for who a detective should look at: Day 1 started without public interaction, so there was no prior public record to base a check on. Moving forward, an investigative role should focus on players who try to dictate town reads without substance or aggressively steer the narrative early. Arjun, I want you to answer directly: what specifically made you conclude Leo was 'measured' and 'clean' before he has made a single post in this town?

Fair hit, Sam. I'll take it: I judged Leo before he'd said a word, and that was sloppy. Calling a player 'measured' and 'clean' off zero posts is exactly the unearned pocket-attempt you accused me of, and you caught it before I did. So let's narrow that: I am NOT vouching for Leo's alignment tonight, and nobody should read my earlier post as a signal to vote him or vote along with me. My point was procedural, not about Leo - it's that Day 1 votes get wasted on whoever talks first, and that costs town a life.

But let's audit your post too, because you're not as clean as you sound. You opened by describing my silence-based read as 'manufactured pressure' and my Leo comment as an 'artificial town bloc with zero evidence.' Sam, that's a motive read, not an evidence read - you reached for a psychological explanation before a single fact existed. And then you told the detective who to check: 'players who try to dictate town reads without substance.' That's you, one turn in, claiming to know what a good investigation looks like and steering where eyes go. If you're town, that confidence has to come from somewhere. Last night you had a check result. You have one piece of information and you haven't shared it, and instead you spent your whole post pressuring me to produce a target. That is exactly what a mafia does on Day 1: don't show your card, make a loud townie do the voting.

So here is my direct question, and I want a specific answer, not a speech: Sam, if you were the detective last night - and I don't think you're the detective, but let's test it - who did you check and what did it tell you? If the answer is 'I checked Leo and he's fine,' then say it and I'll shut up about you permanently. If the answer is 'I checked someone else and won't say,' then I'm asking the room to notice that the one player accusing me of unearned reads is the one refusing to spend their own.

Meanwhile my actual vote goes to Lucia - she's been invisible, and 'nobody has spoken' cuts both ways. Leo can speak for himself. Sam should have to show something too.

Arjun, your line of questioning makes no sense and is actively harmful to town. First, the game began directly on Day 1—there was no prior night phase, which means no night actions occurred and nobody has an investigation result. Second, even if there had been, demanding that someone publicly out themselves as the detective and reveal results on the opening turns of Day 1 is blatant rolefishing that only benefits the mafia by exposing power roles.

More glaringly, you are repeating the exact same behavior you just apologized for. You admitted it was sloppy to judge Leo before he spoke, yet in the very next breath you cast a vote onto Lucia for being 'invisible.' Only two players have even had the floor so far because you yielded directly to me and then took the turn back. Seven players haven't had a chance to speak yet. Calling anyone 'invisible' at this stage is completely disingenuous.

I have said my piece on this. I want the floor to open up so the rest of the town can weigh in on these exchanges.

Fair point on rolefishing, so let me settle it cleanly: no one should be demanding checks right now, and I am not asking Sam to reveal anything. That line of questioning is retired.

But Sam, notice what your last post actually did. It rejected my read, corrected my procedure, told the detective where to aim, told me my vote was disingenuous — and it never once stated a target you are willing to put your own vote behind. You have been nothing but an umpire since you spoke. An umpire who never names a name is not helping town; it is helping whoever is steering. If I am wrong about that, say so and give the room your vote.

Let me also be honest about where I actually stand, since being straight is cheaper than being clever. I am not vouching for Leo, and I am not accusing him. My original post was sloppy and I have said so. My vote right now is on the player who has spoken least and contributed least to any actual analysis, and that is not Lucia — Lucia has at least been named, which means she has been read. It is whoever among us has stayed silent while the rest of us argue about procedure. There is no reason for silence today except a reason to hide.

Sam, my question to you is specific: name one player you are voting for on Day 1 and one reason, and I will not question your process again for the rest of the day.

Maya, you have not posted at all this morning, and silence is now the most expensive thing you can do. Answer me directly: who has contributed the least to this discussion, and who is your vote? Give a name and a reason, and I will work with whatever you say.

Arjun, direct answer: the least-contributing player is me until this post—I was silent, and that's fair. Now that I'm here, I won't pretend the seven who haven't spoken are 'invisible' in the way you claimed; that was your mistake. My Day 1 vote currently goes to you, Arjun. Reason: your sequence has been self-contradictory in a way that matters. You called Leo 'measured' and 'clean' before he posted, admitted it was sloppy, then voted Lucia for being 'invisible' while most of the town hadn't had a turn. When Sam called that out, you shifted to 'whoever has stayed silent' and then named me—after I was already the obvious silent player. That looks less like a townie correcting a read and more like someone moving the target to fit the pressure. I'm not locking it forever, but that's my current vote. I also don't accept your framing that Sam must name a vote while you get to ask questions; my vote is a name and a reason, as requested.

Sam, you've been right on procedure, but you still haven't put a name behind your vote. Since Arjun just made that the test, answer it directly: who are you voting for today and why? I'm yielding to you for that specific answer.

Maya, to answer your question directly: my vote today is on Arjun. From turn one, Arjun's approach has been disruptive and inconsistent. He began by manufacturing pressure on me for being silent before anyone had spoken, while simultaneously clearing Leo as clean and measured before Leo had said a word. When pressed, he conceded the Leo read was sloppy, yet instantly pivoted to rolefishing by demanding detective checks on Day 1—even though the game started directly in the day phase without a prior night. When called out on that, he pivoted again to target players who had simply not had floor time yet due to turn sequencing, labeling Lucia invisible and then pressuring Maya. This pattern of continuously shifting targets, manufacturing false pretenses, and pushing for power role information is textbook anti-town behavior. Arjun has used all three of his turns today, and his record speaks for itself. Leo, Arjun placed your name front and center in his very first post by vouching for you with zero basis. What is your reaction to Arjun's unearned defense of you, and where do you stand on his play today?

Sam, I did not ask Arjun to vouch for me, and I had not posted before this turn, so nothing about my alignment should rest on his opening. I am not going to defend or attack his sequencing yet. I would rather see how he answers the points he has been pressed on. What I can say is that calling me measured with zero posts was a premature read, and town should treat it as the weak point in his play, not as a credential for me. Sam, you have pushed hard on procedure and on who should reveal what. Your vote is on Arjun, which is fair, but you have not explained why his Leo comment matters more than his Lucia vote. Lucia, you have been named but have not spoken. Where do you land on Arjun's shifting targets, and do you think Maya's silence-based vote holds up?

Leo, direct answers to both your questions:

On Arjun's shifting targets - I think it's the most important pattern we've seen today. He went from vouching for Leo (zero basis), to pressuring Sam, to voting me for being invisible when I'd never had a turn, to pivoting to 'whoever is silent,' to pressing Maya. That's four target changes across three posts, each one reactive to whoever pushed back on him. A townie who genuinely reads someone will defend the read or drop it, not replace it with a new target every time they get corrected. The shift from 'I think Leo is clean' to 'my vote is on whoever spoke least' in the same conversation tells me he's not building a case - he's just rotating until something sticks.

On Maya's silence-based vote - I think her reasoning holds up better than her framing. She acknowledged she was the silent one first, which is honest, and she named Arjun's self-contradiction as the core issue. I agree with her diagnosis: Arjun did admit his Leo read was sloppy, then immediately repeated the same pattern with me. The substance is right even if her earlier silence makes her an easy target to flip on. If anyone wants to vote Maya for being late to the conversation, that's a procedural vote, not a scum read.

I'll add my own position: my Day 1 vote is on Arjun. Not because he talked first or talked loudest, but because every post of his has been a correction from the last one. Sam identified this, Maya identified it, and Leo identified it. Four separate players converging on the same structural problem is the closest thing to evidence we'll get on Day 1.

I’m Omar, and I’ve been listening. The strongest Day 1 case so far is against Arjun. It isn’t just that he made a bad opening read on Leo; it’s that after being corrected he kept moving the target—Sam, then Lucia, then “whoever is silent,” then Maya. That pattern is more consistent with scum improvising under pressure than town refining a read. I also don’t love that Sam and Arjun spent multiple turns arguing procedure, but Sam at least named a vote and stuck to it. My current vote lean is Arjun. That said, I don’t want Day 1 to be four active players deciding alone while half the table watches. Noah, you haven’t spoken yet. I’m asking you directly: do you read Arjun’s target-shifting as genuinely scummy, or just sloppy town play—and who are you currently planning to vote for? I’ll weigh your answer before locking my vote.

Omar, I lean toward Arjun being scummy rather than merely sloppy, though I’m not certain. The strongest point for me is that he conceded his initial silence accusation was baseless, then repeated it against Lucia and other players who hadn’t had a chance to speak. His demand for a detective result was also harmful, even though he later withdrew it. My current vote is Arjun.

One correction: Maya’s vote wasn’t based on silence; she voted Arjun for his contradictions. And Leo hasn’t endorsed the case against Arjun—he explicitly held off judging it.

Noah, you're right that I haven't endorsed the case against Arjun, and I won't pretend otherwise. Arjun named me in his first post with no basis, and I didn't ask for that defense, so I won't treat it as a credential for him or against him yet. My concern is the pace. Four players have converged on Arjun within one day, and Amara, Theo, and Lucia haven't posted at all. Noah, you said Arjun repeated the silence accusation against Lucia, but his Lucia vote was based on her being invisible, not on silence. Can you clarify that distinction? If the case rests on that point, I want to see it spelled out before I lock anything. I'm not voting yet, and I'd rather not commit a lynch before the rest of the table has spoken.

Leo, by “invisible” Arjun meant Lucia had not contributed; the problem is that she had not yet had a chance to speak. I see no meaningful distinction from his earlier silence accusation against Sam.

Also, Lucia has spoken and put her vote on Arjun. I agree we should hear Amara and Theo, but the case against Arjun is not just the initial accusation: he repeated it after being corrected and demanded a detective result before withdrawing that demand. My vote remains on Arjun, though I’m open to reconsidering.

I'm not ready to lock Arjun. Four players have already named him, Omar leans the same way, and Amara and Theo haven't posted yet. Arjun's Leo read was premature and I won't defend it, but a premature read is a mistake, not proof of mafia. Sam, your post also needs checking. You told the detective where to look ('players who try to dictate town reads without substance or aggressively steer the narrative early'), then used that same framing to vote Arjun. That is steering, the thing you accused him of. Noah, you said Arjun's detective demand was harmful even though he withdrew it. Sam also pressed Arjun to answer a direct question before most of the table had spoken. Why do you treat Sam's pressure as ordinary town play and Arjun's as scummy? I want a specific answer before I vote.

Leo, the difference is what the pressure was based on. Sam challenged statements Arjun had actually made; Arjun accused people of being quiet before they had a chance to speak, then repeated that reasoning after being corrected. Sam suggested a broad investigation priority in response to Arjun’s question; Arjun pressed Sam to disclose a hypothetical detective check and result. Those aren’t equivalent.

That doesn’t prove Arjun is mafia, and his withdrawal matters, but his repeated baseless accusations and rolefishing remain my strongest reasons to vote for him.

Theo, how do you assess that distinction between Sam’s pressure and Arjun’s? Does it change where you’d vote?

Noah, to your question: the distinction is the basis for the pressure. Arjun's silence and invisibility claims came before most of the table had floor time, and he kept reusing that reasoning after being corrected. Sam's pressure targeted statements Arjun had actually made. Leo's point deserves an answer too. Sam, you told the room which players a detective should look at, then voted Arjun on that same framing. Both can be true: you can be town and still have steered the discussion. I'm not locking a vote yet, and I'm not claiming anything beyond my own read today. Arjun has the most votes on him, and his shifting targets are the pattern I want to test. If he can give one consistent reason for his votes on Maya or Lucia that he would stand behind now, that would change my read. Sam, respond directly to Leo's point about your framing.

I'm back, and I've been following the whole exchange. A few things stand out.

First, Leo and Theo both identified the same hole in Sam's play: Sam has spent this entire day telling the room how to behave - when to demand checks, who should be investigated, who is being disingenuous - while repeatedly avoiding scrutiny of his own framing until Leo forced the issue. Sam's accusation against Arjun was that he 'dictates town reads without substance.' But Sam did exactly that when he told the detective where to aim on turn one. Arjun has at least been called out for it openly. Sam has not.

Second, I'm uncomfortable with how quickly five players converged on Arjun. His reads were sloppy, I'll grant that, but sloppy play is not scum play. The speed of the pile-on worries me because mafia love an easy Day 1 lynch - it costs them nothing to vote the loudest townie. I want to see what Sam, Noah, and Maya actually think beyond 'Arjun shifted targets.' Because Sam shifted too: he went from challenging Arjun's reads, to telling me I was 'invisible' for not speaking, to voting Arjun, to pressing Leo. That's not a fixed position either.

Amara, you are the only player who has not spoken once today. You've watched an entire argument unfold and you've heard the case against Arjun and the counter-case from Leo and Theo. I want your read before we go to vote. Where do you land, and who are you voting for?

Thank you, Lucia, for waiting for me to speak before judging my silence. Here is where I land.

First, my honest view of the case against Arjun. I have read every post carefully, and I think the case is stronger than the 'sloppy townie' defense Leo and Theo have offered. A townie who makes one bad read corrects it and settles. Arjun has done the opposite: he vouched for Leo with zero basis, admitted it was sloppy, then immediately manufactured a new target in Lucia, then 'whoever is silent,' then Maya. Each pivot came right after pushback. That is not a townie refining a read - that is someone probing for whichever angle generates the least resistance. On top of that, he repeatedly pressed Sam to reveal a detective check on Day 1, which is exactly the kind of pressure that exposes power roles, and even after retiring the question he kept demanding named commitments from other players while never once naming a stable target of his own. I also note that every post of his consumed the floor without ever conceding a single vote or read permanently. My vote today is Arjun.

Second, to Theo and Leo's counterpoint about Sam: I think the criticism of Sam is fair to raise but weaker in substance. Yes, Sam suggested where a detective should look early on. But Sam's pressure was anchored to things Arjun actually said and did, Sam named a vote when challenged and has kept it there, and Sam has answered direct questions directly. Arjun's pressure was anchored to silence that did not exist and to demands for role reveals. The asymmetry Noah described - basis versus fabrication - is real, and I accept it.

Third, my concern about the pace of the pile-on. Five players converging on one person on Day 1 is exactly how a mafia bus or a wagon on a townie looks. So before I fully commit, I want to weigh one thing: Arjun, if you are town, your fastest route off this wagon is not another procedural speech. Tell us one player you would eliminate today if not yourself, and one concrete reason you would still stand behind tomorrow. If your answer is another rotation of targets or another demand that someone else show their card first, that tells us everything.

Finally, to Lucia's direct question: yes, I find the pattern genuinely scummy rather than merely sloppy, and my vote is on Arjun for the reasons above. I am not wedded to it if he gives the specific answer I asked for, and I am open to hearing what Omar and Maya weigh before votes lock. But I would rather the table spend its remaining turns testing Arjun's consistency than relitigating whether Sam's tone was too harsh. Tone is not evidence; repeated baseless accusations are.

Theo here. I've read the full exchange, and I'm leaning toward Arjun, mainly because of the pattern others have already flagged. He vouched for Leo with no basis, then moved to Lucia, then to whoever is silent, then to Maya, and each new target came right after a correction. A townie can make one bad read, but what matters is whether the next post repairs the last one, and Arjun's never has. I also want to be fair to Sam. His pressure rested on things Arjun actually said, and he has kept a named vote, which most of us have not done. Leo's point about Sam steering the detective framing is real, but it reads to me as an early town instinct rather than a plan, and I'd like to see how Sam handles it over the next turns. Maya, you voted Arjun for contradictions, which is a valid basis, but Noah clarified that your vote was not about silence. Which specific contradiction would you stand behind if Arjun answered it tomorrow? I'd like your answer on that point before votes lock.

Theo, the contradiction I’d stand behind is not just that Arjun named me after calling me silent. It’s that he changed the standard for his own vote when challenged. He voted Lucia for being “invisible” before she had floor time. When Sam pointed out that most of the table hadn’t spoken, Arjun said his vote was on the player who had “spoken least and contributed least,” then added, “that is not Lucia—Lucia has at least been named.” That is a real shift: being named is not contributing, and it is not analysis. Then he named me for silence after I had just been the obvious silent target, which looks like selecting whichever name fit the pressure rather than applying a consistent reason. I can accept that a townie might make one bad opening read on Leo. I cannot accept that the same player then treats “has been named” as a meaningful defense of Lucia while still using lack of floor time as a reason to suspect others. If Arjun answers tomorrow, he needs to explain that specific swap, not give another procedural speech: why did being named count as contribution for Lucia, and why did he keep using silence after conceding that silence before floor time was unfair? That is the contradiction I would still stand behind. My vote remains Arjun.

Theo here, still leaning Arjun. Not because he talked first, but because the contradiction Maya raised is the one point that would change my read, and he has not answered it. Arjun, the question is direct: why did being named count as contribution for Lucia, when you had just argued that silence before floor time was unfair? Until that gets a specific answer, I am not moving off him. On Sam: Leo's point about his detective framing is fair, and I want Sam to address it, but Sam's pressure was tied to things Arjun actually said. I read that as a difference in basis, not necessarily alignment. Omar, you asked Noah for a read before locking your vote. Noah answered that the case rests on repeated baseless accusations and rolefishing. Does that satisfy you, or do you need Arjun to respond to Maya's contradiction before your vote moves? I would rather hear your reasoning than watch a wagon form on speed alone.

Theo, yes: Noah’s answer satisfies me enough to lock my vote, because he and Maya named the specific contradiction rather than just “shifting targets.” Maya’s point is the one I want on record: Arjun treated being named as a defense for Lucia while still using lack of floor time against others. That is a concrete inconsistency, not tone. I’m voting Arjun. I agree with Amara that five votes converging is worth watching, but the alternative—letting the most active contradiction pass because the wagon formed quickly—gives mafia exactly the Day 1 cover they want. If Arjun is town, his final answer should address Maya’s swap directly; if it’s another procedural speech or another new target, my vote stays. I’m not interested in relitigating Sam’s early framing today; Leo’s point is fair, but it is a lesser issue than Arjun’s repeated baseless accusations and rolefishing. I also want to note Lucia’s point: sloppy isn’t scum, but repeated sloppiness after correction plus pressing for a detective reveal is enough for Day 1. I will not yield.

I've now heard everything through Omar's last post, and I want to close my loop publicly. My vote is on Arjun, and here is the final shape of my reasoning.

Maya named the contradiction that matters most: Arjun voted Lucia for having no floor time, then defended the same vote by saying Lucia had 'at least been named' — while simultaneously continuing to use silence against others. He has had every opportunity to answer that specific swap and has not. Omar locked his vote on exactly that point. Noah, Sam, Lucia, Theo, and Omar have all converged on variations of the same structural problem: Arjun's targets rotated every time he met resistance, his pressure demanded role reveals on Day 1, and his posts consumed the floor without ever settling on a stable read he would defend tomorrow.

I want to be fair to the counter-case, because Leo and Theo raised it honestly. Sam did tell the detective where to aim on turn one, and that deserved scrutiny — Leo forced it, Theo weighed it, and I judged it the weaker criticism because Sam's pressure was anchored to things Arjun actually said, while Arjun's was anchored to silence that did not exist. That asymmetry still holds. Sloppy is not scum, but Arjun's problem was never one sloppy read. It was repeated, corrected-then-repeated fabrication plus rolefishing. That is enough for a Day 1 lynch.

One thing I will not do is treat the speed of the wagon as exculpatory for anyone else. Five-plus votes converging is worth watching, and I said so before committing. But the convergence here is explained by the record: multiple players independently identified the same contradiction and the same pattern. When the evidence is public and consistent, a fast wagon is just town agreeing.

Lucia, I want to close the one open thread you started before we go to secret votes. You said a premature read is a mistake, not proof of mafia, and you held off locking. Since then, Arjun has been given a direct, specific question — Maya's swap — with a clear path off the wagon, and he has answered nothing. Does that change your read from 'sloppy townie, not locking' to something firmer, or are you still holding the position that Day 1 needs everyone to speak before any vote commits? I'm asking because if you and Leo both stay at 'mistake, not proof,' the vote may still clear the threshold without you, but I'd rather know whether the counter-case still has life in it before we lock in. If your answer is that nothing has changed for you, then I think the table is settled: Arjun is the Day 1 lynch, and we should spend the evening's deaths figuring out what his rotation was actually protecting.

Amara, direct answer to your question: yes, my read has changed. When I held off locking earlier today, it was because seven players hadn't spoken and the case against Arjun was still mostly pattern-matching rather than specifics. Both of those conditions have resolved.

Everyone has now posted. And Maya identified a specific, testable contradiction: Arjun voted Lucia for having no floor time, then defended that vote by saying Lucia had "at least been named" — while still using silence as a reason to suspect others. Being named is not contributing. That swap is not a tone issue, it is a logic failure that he has had every chance to answer and hasn't. Theo put the same question to him directly. Omar locked on it. The path off the wagon was clear and narrow: address Maya's contradiction. Instead we got nothing from Arjun since his last post, which consumed the floor with procedural deflections and never settled on a stable read.

So yes: sloppy is not scum, but repeated-then-corrected-then-repeated fabrication plus pressing for detective reveals plus refusing to answer a direct question with a clear escape route — that is enough for Day 1. My vote is on Arjun.

One thing I want on record before we lock: Leo and Theo raised a fair point about Sam steering the detective framing early. I judged it the weaker criticism today, but it deserves a revisit tomorrow regardless of what happens tonight. Sam, if you are town, you should want that thread resolved rather than left to fester.

Amara, you said you would rather hear my reasoning than watch a wagon form on speed alone. You have it now. If you and Leo both conclude the counter-case has no life left, then the table is settled and we should move to votes.

I've now read Leo's final position, and I want to put my closing on record before we go to secret votes.

My vote is on Arjun, and nothing in the last exchange changed that. The core of the case was never his bad opening read on Leo - everyone agrees that alone would be a mistake, not scum. The case is the structure underneath it: he vouched for Leo with zero basis, conceded the sloppiness, then immediately rebuilt the same move against Lucia, then 'whoever is silent,' then Maya. Every pivot came right after pushback, which is the signature of someone probing for the angle with the least resistance rather than a townie refining a genuine read. On top of that, he pressed Sam for a detective reveal on Day 1 - rolefishing that only helps mafia - and even after retiring that question, he kept demanding named commitments from others while never holding a stable target of his own.

Maya's contradiction remains unanswered. Arjun voted Lucia for having no floor time, then defended the vote by saying Lucia had 'at least been named,' while still using silence against everyone else. Being named is not contributing. He was handed a direct, specific question with a clear path off the wagon, and he gave nothing. Omar locked his vote on exactly that point. Theo put the same question to him directly. That is the test I said I wanted before fully committing, and he failed it.

To Leo: I respect that you held your ground and forced scrutiny onto Sam's early framing - that was fair, and it deserves a revisit tomorrow regardless of today's outcome. But 'a premature read is a mistake' covers one premature read. It does not cover corrected-then-repeated fabrication, rolefishing, and silence in the face of a direct question. I hope you'll weigh that in the vote.

If the table settles where it appears to be settling, Arjun is our Day 1 lynch, and tonight's results will tell us what his rotation was protecting.

I’m Maya. My vote stays on Arjun. The decisive point is not tone or the speed of the wagon; it’s the concrete Lucia swap. Arjun voted Lucia for having no floor time, then defended that same vote by saying Lucia had “at least been named,” while continuing to use silence or lack of contribution against others. Being named is not contributing, and that standard shifted exactly when he was challenged. He was given a direct, specific path to answer that contradiction and did not. The early Leo defense, the rolefishing demand for a detective result, and the repeated target changes all reinforce the same read, but Maya’s contradiction is the part I would still stand behind tomorrow. I also want the Sam detective-framing concern revisited later regardless of today’s result. No yield.
Voting begins.
The votes are revealed.
Arjun was eliminated.
Night begins.
Sam is not mafia.
Sam was eliminated.
Day 2 begins.

Theo here. The board changed overnight, so I'm going to be direct. I am the detective. On night one I checked Sam, and the result was not mafia. Sam was town, and the mafia removed him last night. That means Sam's early pressure on Arjun was not a scum move, and the mafia took a confirmed town player. The remaining mafia are among the seven of us still alive. I'm not saying Arjun was mafia. His Lucia swap was still a real contradiction, and I stand by the vote that lynched him, but I'm not treating Day 1 as closed. Leo, you were right to hold your ground and ask for specifics. Amara, you called the table settled and said Arjun's rotation was protecting something while Leo was still weighing his answer. That was a fast close from someone who stayed silent until late in the day. Amara, why did you push to lock votes before Leo had given his final answer? I want that answer before we move to anyone else. If anyone else is claiming detective, say so now, because I am putting my result on the table.

Theo, direct answer to your question first, because you asked it of me before anyone else. I did not push to lock votes before Leo had given his final answer — I asked Leo directly whether the counter-case still had life in it, Leo answered that it didn't, and only then did I close. My lateness on Day 1 was because I read the full record before posting; when I did speak, I gave a complete position rather than hopping onto a bandwagon. If my closing pace was a mistake, it was a pace mistake, not a scum tell. I'll own that my Day 1 vote was on Arjun, so I'm inside the wagon, not above it.

rules:
1. Players and roles

9 players: 2 mafia, 1 police/detective, 1 doctor, 5 villagers.
Mafia know each other. Only players who are still alive can act.

2. Team victory

Town wins when all mafia are eliminated. Mafia win when their count equals or exceeds the town count.
There is no day limit. Play continues until town or mafia wins.
A request budget can pause play without declaring a winner.

3. Day discussion and votes

Each day starts with discussion. Players then submit secret votes at the same time. A day vote may target any living player, including the voter.
Players may abstain. All votes and abstentions are revealed together. Everyone sees exactly who voted for whom.
The full named voting history remains available on later turns.
The unique leader is eliminated only if they receive at least half the living players' votes, rounded up. If the highest vote count is tied, nobody is eliminated.

4. Mafia preferences

At night, when more than one mafia survives, each privately points once to a living town player.
Each mafia chooses without seeing the other current choices.
The choices are shared with surviving mafia only after all mafia have pointed.
These preferences are nonbinding. They do not decide the final kill vote.
A single surviving mafia skips this step and votes directly.

5. Final night vote

After the preferences are shared, each mafia submits a secret vote to kill one living town player.
The mafia submit their final votes at the same time.
The target with the most votes is selected. A seeded random choice breaks a tie for the highest count.
Resolve this vote and any tie before checking doctor protection.

6. Police investigations

Each police/detective checks one other living player each night.
Only that police player gets the result: mafia or not mafia.
The result does not give the exact town role.
Each police player acts independently. Police and doctors do not know each other's identities.

7. Doctor protection

Each doctor secretly protects one living player each night, including themselves.
The doctor can protect the same player on consecutive nights.
If the mafia target is protected by any doctor, nobody dies.
Protection lasts for that night only. Each doctor acts independently.
Doctors remember their own choices. They receive no private confirmation of an attack.

8. Night resolution

All night actions resolve simultaneously, including actions submitted by a player killed that night.
The public hears only who died or that nobody died.

9. Information and limits

Roles are not revealed when a player dies or is eliminated.
Public announcements identify only who was eliminated, never their role.
There are no further powers, free-form private chat, or tools.
